verses.english: Linked Discourses 3.24
3. Kosala
Archery
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Seated to one side, King Pasenadi said to the Buddha,
“Sir, where should a gift be given?”
“Wherever your heart feels inspired, great king.”
“But sir, where is a gift very fruitful?”

verses.pali: “Aññaṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, kattha dānaṁ dātabbaṁ, aññaṁ panetaṁ kattha dinnaṁ mahapphalanti?
verses.english: “Where a gift should be given is one thing, great king, but where a gift is very fruitful is another.

verses.pali: Sīlavato kho, mahārāja, dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, no tathā dussīle.
verses.english: A gift is very fruitful when it’s given to an ethical person, not so much to an unethical person.

verses.pali: Tena hi, mahārāja, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā, te khameyya, tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
verses.english: Well then, great king, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.
What do you think, great king?

verses.pali: idha tyassa yuddhaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ saṅgāmo samupabyūḷho.
verses.english: Suppose you were at war, ready to fight a battle.

verses.pali: Atha āgaccheyya khattiyakumāro asikkhito akatahattho akatayoggo akatūpāsano bhīru chambhī utrāsī palāyī.
verses.english: Then along comes an aristocrat youth who is untrained, inexpert, unfit, inexperienced. And he’s fearful, scared, nervous, quick to flee.

verses.pali: Bhareyyāsi taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca te tādisena purisenā”ti?
verses.english: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

verses.pali: “Nāhaṁ, bhante, bhareyyaṁ taṁ purisaṁ, na ca me attho tādisena purisenā”ti.
verses.english: “No, sir, I would have no use for such a man.”
“What about a brahmin youth,
a peasant youth,
or a menial youth who was similar?”

verses.pali: na ca me attho tādisena purisenā”ti.
verses.english: “No, sir, I would have no use for such a man.”

verses.pali: idha tyassa yuddhaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ saṅgāmo samupabyūḷho.
verses.english: Suppose you were at war, ready to fight a battle.

verses.pali: Atha āgaccheyya khattiyakumāro susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano abhīru acchambhī anutrāsī apalāyī.
verses.english: Then along comes an aristocrat youth who is trained, expert, fit, experienced. And he’s fearless, brave, bold, standing his ground.

verses.pali: Bhareyyāsi taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca te tādisena purisenā”ti?
verses.english: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

verses.pali: “Bhareyyāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca me tādisena purisenā”ti.
verses.english: “Yes, sir, I would have a use for such a man.”
“What about a brahmin youth,
a peasant youth,

verses.pali: atha āgaccheyya suddakumāro susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano abhīru acchambhī anutrāsī apalāyī.
verses.english: or a menial youth who was similar?

verses.pali: Bhareyyāsi taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca te tādisena purisenā”ti?
verses.english: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

verses.pali: “Bhareyyāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca me tādisena purisenā”ti.
verses.english: “Yes, sir, I would have a use for such a man.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, mahārāja, yasmā kasmā cepi kulā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti, so ca hoti pañcaṅgavippahīno pañcaṅgasamannāgato, tasmiṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti.
verses.english: “In the same way, a gift to anyone who has given up five factors and possesses five factors is very fruitful, no matter what family they’ve gone forth from.
What are the five factors they’ve given up?

verses.pali: Kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti.
verses.english: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
These are the five factors they’ve given up.
What are the five factors they possess?

verses.pali: Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti.
verses.english: The entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.
These are the five factors they possess.
I say that a gift to anyone who has given up these five factors and possesses these five factors is very fruitful.”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Any youth skilled at archery,
powerful and vigorous,
would be employed by a king going to war—
one is not a coward by reason of birth.
Just so, whoever is settled
in the qualities of patience and gentleness,
a clever person with noble conduct,
should be venerated even if they’re low born.
You should build lovely hermitages
and settle learned people in them.
You should set up water supplies in barren regions
and passages in places hard to travel.
Food, drink, edibles,
clothes, and lodgings
should be given to the upright ones,
with a clear and confident heart.
The thundering rain cloud,
its hundred peaks wreathed in lightning,
pours down over the rich earth,
soaking the uplands and valleys.
So too an astute person,
faithful and learned,
should prepare a meal to satisfy
supplicants with food and drink.
Rejoicing, they strew gifts about,
crying ‘Give! give!’
For that is their thunder,
like rain sent from the heavens.
That stream of merit so abundant
showers down on the giver.”
